Clients Blackbox is a performance marketing agency specializing in Meta advertising for Registered Investment Advisors.

We help financial advisors grow their practices by generating qualified appointments with high-net-worth prospects. Our proven video sales letter methodology has generated more than $45 billion in AUM pipeline for financial advisors across the country.

We operate with a performance-first mindset. Our clients hire us to deliver qualified appointments at a specific cost per appointment, with target show rates and close rates that make the economics work for their practice. Clients Blackbox is in a major growth period, and we're looking for a Paid Media Strategist / Account Strategist who can own client accounts from strategy through execution.

The Opportunity

This is a hands-on strategist role with responsibility for both client relationships and campaign performance. You'll own a portfolio of accounts, lead bi-weekly client calls, manage Meta campaigns, monitor results, contribute to ad messaging, and serve as the primary point of contact for your clients.

You'll report to the Associate Director of Operations and be directly accountable for client results, relationships, and retention.

What You'll Own

*Client Strategy & Relationships*

* Own a portfolio of client accounts and serve as the primary point of contact
* Lead bi-weekly client calls covering performance, strategy, priorities, and next steps
* Prepare and send bi-weekly performance reports at least 24 hours before scheduled calls
* Translate campaign data into clear, actionable recommendations for non-technical clients
* Build strong client relationships that support retention, renewals, and referrals
* Solve account issues proactively to support stability and growth

*Meta Campaign Management*

* Build, launch, and optimize Meta campaigns focused on lead generation and appointment booking
* Manage budgets, audience targeting, bid strategies, creative testing, and campaign variables
* Monitor performance daily and make adjustments based on cost-per-appointment and other key metrics
* Diagnose underperforming campaigns and develop strategies to improve results
* Test audiences, messaging, and creative to identify opportunities for stronger performance
* Contribute to ad copy and campaign messaging

*Tracking & Technical Execution*

* Set up and troubleshoot tracking, Meta pixels, and conversion events
* Configure Calendly integrations, Zapier automations, and lead-routing workflows
* Resolve technical issues between advertising platforms and client systems
* Proactively monitor tracking and lead flow to prevent issues from affecting client results

  
**Requirements**  

* 4+ years of hands-on paid media experience, with a strong focus on Meta advertising
* Experience simultaneously managing multiple client accounts and leading client-facing conversations
* Proven ability to manage campaigns toward defined performance targets while supporting client retention
* Experience with conversion tracking, pixels, and basic marketing automation
* Strong communication, organization, and problem-solving skills

**Preferred Experience**

* Financial services marketing
* Lead-generation and appointment-setting campaigns
* Video sales letter marketing
* High-ticket or considered-purchase funnels
* Direct-response advertising

* Paid Time Off, including vacation, sick time, and public holidays
* Training & Development
* Work From Home
* Flexible Schedule
* Performance Bonus

jobs.title: Growth Marketing Analyst
jobs.description:
**About Think Sensory**

Think Sensory is an online education platform for therapists, educators, and parents supporting neurodivergent children. We offer continuing education for pediatric therapists and educators, self-paced courses, printable resources, and articles. Think Sensory is an AOTA Approved Provider.

Our flagship program is the Think Sensory Summit, a virtual event featuring interview-style sessions with experts and advocates in occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, psychology, education, and the neurodiversity movement. Season 2 runs in November 2026. Three summits are planned for 2027, starting with a summit for teachers in the spring.

All of our work is grounded in neuroaffirming practice.

**About the Role**

We're hiring a Growth Marketing Analyst to drive insights and recommendations on marketing performance across our digital channels. This is an entry-level role, and recent graduates are encouraged to apply.

The role sits at the intersection of marketing and analytics. You'll translate campaign data into actionable insights that improve lead acquisition and conversion performance, using AI-enabled tools to speed up the analysis.

We're looking for a self-starter with a strong analytical mindset, a passion for learning and growth, and a shared commitment to supporting neurodivergent children.

We're a small, growing team, and this role will grow with the company.

You'll report directly to our President and work closely with our President and CEO.

**Key Responsibilities**

Campaign Performance and Insights

* Analyze performance across our digital channels, including paid social, email, and our website
* Help set performance targets and benchmarks, such as conversion rates, engagement, and the share of free registrations that upgrade to a paid pass
* Evaluate lead generation across channels, including volume, quality, and conversion through the funnel
* Identify the key drivers of conversions, cost per acquisition, and overall campaign results
* Translate findings into actionable recommendations, including improvements to audience targeting, messaging, and timing
* Report weekly to our President on performance, trends, and recommendations

Lifecycle and Retention

* Analyze the customer lifecycle across summits, including upgrade rates, retention, and repeat registrations
* Identify opportunities to re-engage past registrants and improve retention

Channel and Budget Support

* Monitor performance across our owned channels, including our website, email, and checkout
* Provide insight into channel performance to inform budget allocation
* Identify opportunities to scale high-performing campaigns or improve efficiency
* Support forecasting and performance planning

Marketing Support

* Schedule and support email and organic social campaigns, including summit launch sequences
* Respond to social media comments
* Assist with paid social campaign setup and monitoring

**Required Qualifications**

* A bachelor’s degree in a field such as accounting, economics, statistics, math, business, marketing, or psychology
* Comfortable working with spreadsheets, numbers, and large amounts of data
* Ability to translate data into clear business insights and recommendations
* Detail-oriented, with a strong focus on data accuracy and documentation
* Strong communication and cross-functional collaboration skills
* Self-motivated, with the ability to take initiative and work with minimal supervision in a remote role
* Open to feedback and quick to learn new tools

**Preferred Experience**

* Previous experience in analytics
* Digital marketing experience, or exposure to tools like Meta Ads Manager
* A personal or professional connection to the neurodivergent community, such as lived experience, family, coursework, or work with children, and familiarity with neuroaffirming practices
* Experience at a startup or small business, including part-time jobs, internships, or campus roles

**The Ideal Candidate**

The ideal candidate is curious about what drives results and uses data to find the answer. They’re accurate and thorough, and they communicate findings clearly, including what isn’t working and what they recommend next.

They learn quickly, take ownership of their work, and adapt well in a small, growing company where priorities can shift quickly. They’re looking to build their skills in a role with real opportunity for growth.

They share our respect for neurodivergent people, and that respect shows in how they speak to and about our audience.

**How We Use AI**

Think Sensory is an AI-forward company. We support the use of AI tools to increase efficiency and productivity. In this role, that includes analyzing data, informing decisions, optimizing campaigns, and generating ideas.

The time AI saves goes back into creating content for our audience ourselves. Our ad copy, graphics, and emails are all written and designed by our team, and we expect them to be original and consistent with the Think Sensory brand.

**Work Arrangement**

* Fully remote, open to candidates across the United States
* Flexible schedule: set your own working hours, with availability for scheduled meetings with our President and CEO
* 30 hours per week, with potential to increase as we grow

**Compensation**

$50,000 to $58,000 USD based on 30 hours per week. Compensation is commensurate with experience.

**Application Requirements**

Please include the following with your application:

* Resume
* Cover letter telling us why this work interests you and any connection you have to the neurodivergent community

Think Sensory welcomes applications from neurodivergent and disabled candidates. Accommodations are available at any stage of the hiring process upon request.

Pay: $50,000.00 - $58,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule
* Professional development assistance

Work Location: Remote

jobs.title: Social Media Associate
jobs.description:
**About us:**

Kiva is a global nonprofit, founded in 2005, with a mission to expand financial access and help underserved communities thrive. Kiva unlocks capital for borrowers through crowdfunded loans supported by individuals around the world. Lenders on Kiva can start with as little as $25 to support causes that matter most to them, whether that's gender equity and support for women, refugees, climate change, small businesses, agriculture, and more. Since our founding, over two million people have invested **over $2 billion** in real dreams and real opportunity, spanning more than **100 countries** and **over 5 million** borrowers

As we work toward our mission, Kiva invests in building and retaining a global team of talent to add to our values-driven and digital-first culture. Our organization is supported by over 700 volunteers and 130+ full time employees dispersed around the world, as well as within team hubs located in San Francisco, Nairobi, Bogota, and Bangkok. Kiva's team is growing as we pursue exciting new opportunities to scale our impact and create a financially inclusive world.

#### **Kiva's values:**

Impact first - This is why we exist. This is the drumbeat we march to. Every day.

Extreme ownership - Own it; you, your relationships, your impact. Insist that others support you and hold you accountable.

Be curious and bold - Never stop learning. Question assumptions. Take Risks and dream big.

Inclusion. Equity. Diversity. - Without reservation and without caveat. In our hiring, in our workplace and in our impact in the world.

Honor and integrity - Do the most right thing in the most right way. Cherish diversity and respect each other.

Love and kindness always - Say what you mean. Mean what you say. And don't say it mean. Clarity. Courage. Kindness.

**Role overview:**

The **Social Media Associate** plays a pivotal role in amplifying Kiva's mission, advancing its brand, and maximizing engagement across digital channels. This role is responsible for developing and executing a comprehensive social media strategy that resonates with Kiva's diverse audiences and supports cross-functional goals.

Partnering closely with the Sr. Manager of Growth and Lifecycle, this individual will oversee day-to-day content planning, creation, and scheduling; leverage data and trends to optimize channel performance; and ensure Kiva's digital presence is consistent, engaging, and aligned with organizational priorities. With a mix of creativity, data-savviness, and cross-team collaboration, this role ensures Kiva remains at the forefront of digital storytelling and community engagement.

Kiva's primary social media channels are Instagram & Facebook. Once onboarded, the Social Media Associate will make recommendations for potential channel expansions to YouTube, Pinterest, Reddit, TikTok, or others.

This role works closely with the Creative team to plan engaging and informative content to share on our channels. The Social Media Associate will not be expected to design art assets for our channels, although design skills would be a plus.

At this time, we can only consider applicants with authorization to work in the United States on a permanent, full-time basis; unfortunately we cannot provide visa sponsorship.

**Key responsibilities include:**

**Strategy and Content Management– 40%**

* Help define our strategy for oursocial media profiles, bringing them all into compliance with best practices and recommending a scheduling cadence for each.
* Work with Sr. Manager to build a program to maintain relationships with paid influencers, encouraging organic participation and deepening partnerships.
* Work closely with Sr. Manager to support our paid social media goals through our organic channels and gain efficiencies in content creation across paid and owned social.
* Plan, pitch, and manage the design and copywriting process of new content for our organic social media channels.
* Build organic strategy for expanding to new channels in partnership with Sr. Manager, in service of our growth and lifecycle goals.
* Coordinate with the Creative team Project Manager to source evergreen assets, with the Communications Manager to source Kiva blogs, thought leadership narratives, and impact report assets, and use all content types to build and execute content schedules across platforms.
* Participate in annual marketing campaign planning such as Giving Tuesday and donation drives, adapting campaign content to Kiva's social media channels.
* Maintain an understanding of each channel's algorithm changes, ensuring that we adapt our content and strategies as the platforms evolve.
* Keep each social profile organized, up-to-date and presentable, including managing pinned or featured posts, about sections, and developing new content that makes it easy for new users to understand who Kiva is.

**Social Publishing & Scheduling – 30%**

* Serve as the administrator of Kiva's Sprout social account to manage social media post scheduling, trend tracking, and performance reporting.
* Document planned posts on the Growth & Lifecycle team's content calendar, ensuring clear communication across our various marketing channels.
* Ensure correct copy, tagging, formatting, links, and accessibility best practices (e.g., alt text).
* Maintain accuracy in publishing calendar and flag gaps or inconsistencies.

**Community Monitoring & Engagement – 10%**

* Monitor Sprout Smart Inbox daily for comments, messages, and mentions.
* Respond to routine inquiries and comments in alignment with brand voice and guidelines.
* Engage with relevant page interactions to support visibility and audience growth.
* Consult with the Communications team when needed to escalate comments or DMs to the correct person at Kiva.

**Performance Reporting – 20%**

* Compile monthly social performance reports across platforms.
* Track core metrics (reach, engagement, follower growth, CTR, top-performing posts).
* Share insights with the Growth & Lifec

jobs.title: Asst./Assoc. Copywriter, Creative Marketing - A&F Co. (Remote)
jobs.description:
**Job Description:**

The role of Assistant or Associate Copywriter on the Abercrombie Kids team will focus on developing creative marketing concepts and copy across weekly emails, site content, paid media, and podcast scripts. The ability to create a concise narrative is required—conveying a fashion perspective that reflects the brand’s effortless and elevated positioning, while resonating with the appropriate audience. In addition to writing, this role collaborates closely with design, strategy and merchandising teams to understand customer insights, ensure accuracy of product priorities and demonstrate brand/product differentiators. Successful candidates will have a relentless passion for fashion as well as for our brands, a strong knowledge of copywriting and applicable experience in marketing, preferably retail. All A&F copywriters must possess near-perfect editing and grammar skills and be able to write succinct, clever, on-brand copy that has a clear point of view and a recognizable voice. The ideal applicant is curious, optimistic and highly collaborative while also maintaining a self-starter mindset.

**What will you be doing?**

* Writing weekly marking emails for abercrombie kids and baby/toddler
* Creating consistent editorial copy and incorporating voice across all touchpoints
* Balancing editorial copy with technical product copy, promo language, navigational copy
* Working closely with seasonal team to ensure follow-through from campaign messaging
* Maintaining constant communication with weekly team to ensure quality and consistency
* Ensuring legal compliance of product claims in copy + meeting customer expectations
* Writing longer-form script copy for podcasts, paid media, and video platforms
* Helping create unique, ownable product names for kids OPM (on-product marketing)
* Writing editorial/romanticized language to define collections and key items on-product
* Staying on top of fashion trends and language, including competitor sites/emails
* Editing copy based on leadership feedback, changes to product, trends, performance, etc.
* Staying curious and up-to-date on fashion trends and industry standard language
* Performing and sharing competitive research with the team to inform copy going forward
* Participating in team collaborations to strengthen the culture, share knowledge and serve as the subject matter expert for email marketing

**What will you need to bring?**

* All A&F copywriters must possess near-perfect editing and grammar skills and be able to write short, smart, snappy copy that has a clear point of view and a recognizable voice
* Bachelor's degree, preferably in English, Creative Writing or Advertising/ Copywriting, or related experience
* Basic knowledge of marketing principles
* A relentless passion for fashion and working knowledge of retail/product terminology
* 1+ years of copywriting experience, preferably retail
* A portfolio showcasing your creative writing, technical ability, relentless attention to detail and grammar proficiency - please include any relevant samples of your work
* Strong written/verbal communication & exceptional editing skills
* Seamless ability to operate autonomously with strong time management skills
* Ability to multitask and meet tight deadlines in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment
* Open to constructive criticism in collaborative environments and can quickly action upon
* An ongoing interest in fashion and familiarity with our brand/competitors
* Working knowledge of Microsoft Office, Excel, and Teams is mandatory, experience with Mural, AirTable and Figma is helpful but not required

**Benefits & Perks**

As an Abercrombie & Fitch Co. (A&F Co.) associate, you’ll be eligible to participate in a variety of benefit programs designed to fit you and your lifestyle. A&F is committed to providing simple, competitive, and comprehensive benefits that align with our Company’s culture and values, but most importantly – with you! We also provide competitive incentives to reward the commitment our associates have for moving our global business forward:

* Incentive bonus program
* 401(K) savings plan with company match
* Annual companywide review process
* Flexible spending accounts
* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* Life and disability insurance
* Associate assistance program
* Paid parental and adoption leave
* Access to fertility and adoption benefits through Carrot
* Access to mental health and wellness app, Headspace
* Paid Caregiver Leave
* Mobile Stipend
* Paid time off & one paid volunteer day per year, allowing you to give back to your community
* Work from anywhere (Mondays and Fridays are “work from anywhere” days for most roles & six work from anywhere weeks per year)
* Seven associate wellness half days per year
* Onsite fitness center
* Merchandise discount on all of our brands
* Opportunities for career advancement, we believe in promoting from within
* Access to multiple Associate Resource Groups
* Global team of people who will celebrate you for being YOU!

**Company Description**

Abercrombie & Fitch Co. (A&F Co.) is a global, digitally led omnichannel specialty retailer of apparel and accessories catering to kids through millennials with assortments curated for their specific lifestyle needs.

The company operates a family of brands, including Abercrombie brands and Hollister brands, each sharing a commitment to offer products of enduring quality and exceptional comfort that support global customers on their journey to being and becoming who they are. Abercrombie & Fitch Co. operates stores under these brands across North America, Europe, Asia and the Middle East, as well as the e-commerce sites abercrombie.com, abercrombiekids.com and hollisterco.com.

Learn more about A&F Co. by visiting our corporate website here.

**ABERCROMBIE & FITCH CO. IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER.**

jobs.title: Marketing & Publicity Associate - YA
jobs.description:
Love YA books and talking about them? We’re looking for a rising publishing pro who wants to create compelling campaigns to reach new readers and turn must-read teen books into bestsellers. Sourcebooks, home to award-winning and bestselling children’s books, is looking for a **Marketing and Publicity Associate** to join our dynamic team.  
  
This is a perfect next step for someone currently working at the assistant or coordinator level in publishing who is eager to take on more ownership, creativity, and strategic collaboration. As a Marketing and Publicity Associate, you’ll join marketing and publicity efforts for our YA list across imprints. From long-range campaigns to digital marketing and influencer outreach, you’ll help books thrive in the marketplace and reach readers in meaningful ways.  
  
You’ll gain visibility into every part of the publishing and marketing pipeline, working closely with sales, digital, retail, and editorial teams. You’ll also build strong relationships with authors and the broader children’s book community through events, media placements, and grassroots promotions.  
  
This is an hourly, non-exempt position with a pay range of $23.25 - $25.96. We determine starting pay based on a thorough evaluation of job-related factors, including geographic location, market conditions, relevant experience, training, and education. This process ensures a fair and competitive salary that aligns with both the company and the candidate’s qualifications.  
  
The location for this position can be hybrid or remote in New York or Naperville, Illinois or remote based in any of the following states: Arizona, Connecticut, Illinois, Louisiana, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Montana, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, Washington D.C., and Wisconsin.  
  
**What You’ll Do:**

* Create digital content for Sourcebooks frontlist and backlist YA titles
* Support planning and execute social media marketing initiatives
* Own and grow influencer program for mailings, events, and other partnerships
* Coordinate newsletter features
* Represent marketing efforts to authors, help them develop their social media presence and branding
* Develop press materials and pitch for seasonal and round-up opportunities
* Attend select reader conventions throughout the year
* Collaborate with the marketing and publicity teams to form creative, full-rounded campaigns

**What You Bring:**  
We’re looking for someone who’s ready to level up and lead, with a mix of creative vision and tactical execution.

* 2-3+ years of experience in book publishing, digital marketing, publicity, or a related field
* Strong writing skills and confidence in creating engaging social content
* Adept at designing online graphics and using tools such as Canva and Photoshop
* Ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines with attention to detail
* Keen understanding of the importance of teen books
* Enthusiasm for collaboration on multi-faceted campaigns
* Comfort presenting your ideas and plans to internal and external partners
* Love for books and belief in their power to change lives

**Why** **Sourcebooks****?**  
As Newsweek’s #2 Most Loved Workplace in 2024 and a recognized leader in innovation by Fast Company (2024 Most Innovative Companies, 2023 Best Workplaces for Innovators), we use a mission-driven, data-centered approach to drive success for our authors and their books. We’re a thriving entrepreneurial company that creates books that transcend categories and defy odds, and we’ve been honored with hundreds of national bestsellers and awards. We are passionate book lovers dedicated to connecting books to readers in innovative ways. Story by story, book by book, we have changed more than 300 million lives. Join us as we change 300 million more!  
  
**Ready to Apply:**  
Please submit your resume, salary requirements, and cover letter detailing your relevant experience and interest in this role. Applications without a cover letter will not be considered. Show us your passion and creativity — we’re looking for someone who’s as enthusiastic about this opportunity as we are!  
  
Full-time employees are eligible for our comprehensive benefits program. Our range of benefits include, but are not limited to, Medical/Prescription drug insurance, Dental, Vision, Health Care, Dependent Care, Flexible Spending Account, Health Savings Account 401(k), Short and Long-Term Disability Insurance, Life/AD&D Insurance, & generous paid time off.  
  
Sourcebooks values the array of talents and perspectives that a diverse workforce brings. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, religion, age, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or protected veteran status.

jobs.title: Manager, Paid Search
jobs.description:
At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centred creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. As a global agency, we provide a full suite of services across healthcare communications and marketing to our clients, including top players in the pharmaceutical and biotech industries.

Our #LifeatRealChem culture is rooted in our people—we believe we are best together and are committed to excellence for both our clients and colleagues. Whether you're a seasoned professional or just starting your career, if you share our passion for healthcare and connection, we invite you to explore our opportunities.

Discover your purpose. Embrace innovation. Experience #LifeatRealChem.

Real Chemistry is looking for a **Manager, Paid Search** to join our growing Biddable Media team!

A Manager, Paid Search is responsible for the end-to-end execution, performance, and day-to-day management of paid search campaigns across assigned accounts. This individual translates client objectives into tactical campaign strategies, owns campaign optimization and budget management, identifies opportunities for account growth, and communicates performance insights and recommendations to clients and internal stakeholders. The Manager also coordinates day-to-day projects and begins developing leadership skills by delegating work, overseeing campaign execution, and mentoring junior team members.

This is a hybrid role, based in any of our US offices—including New York City, Boston, Chicago, Carmel, Lambertville, or San Francisco—or remotely within the US, depending on team and business needs.

**What You'll Do**

jobs.title: Senior Social Media Manager
jobs.description:
**Welcome to the Agentic Commerce Era**
=======================================

At Commerce, our mission is to empower businesses to innovate, grow, and thrive with our open, AI-driven commerce ecosystem. As the parent company of BigCommerce , Feedonomics , and Makeswift , we connect the tools and systems that power growth, enabling businesses to unlock the full potential of their data, deliver seamless and personalized experiences across every channel, and adapt swiftly to an ever-changing market. We believe in harnessing AI responsibly to unlock new possibilities, and we’re looking for individuals who use it intentionally to solve problems, accelerate outcomes, and expand what’s possible in their role. Our purpose is to help businesses confidently solve complex commerce challenges so they can build smarter, adapt faster, and grow on their own terms. If you want to be part of a team of bold builders, sharp thinkers, and technical trailblazers who shape the future of commerce, this is the place for you.

The **Senior Social Media Manager** owns the organic social media across our family of brands — Commerce, BigCommerce, Feedonomics, and Makeswift — plus social support for select members of our leadership team.

  

This is an ownership role, not a support role. It sets the strategy, builds the calendar, makes the content, publishes it, and answers for the numbers. Partners with Creative, PR, Demand Gen, Content, and Product Marketing teams, but it shapes and owns the Social Media program.

  

The person who does well here is a strategist who is also fast with their hands. They can build a quarter-long narrative for our brands, and can also turn a keynote clip into a live post the same afternoon without waiting on anyone.

  

**What You'll Do**
------------------

  

**Strategy And Planning**

* Own a documented organic social strategy for each brand, with a clear point of view on what each channel is for and which audiences it serves (customers, prospects, partners, analysts, candidates, employees).
* Maintain a rolling four-week content calendar covering every brand and channel, extended and refreshed weekly, visible to stakeholders.
* Set and defend the content mix: executive video, customer stories, product and platform news, events, recruiting, and reactive commentary.
* Bring a quarterly plan to leadership that connects social activity to brand, demand, and communications goals.
Work alongside a new social selling agency we will deploy  

  

**Content Creation And Publishing**

* Write and edit for social: captions, threads, short-form video scripts, and executive posts that hold each brand's distinct voice.
* Produce your own assets. Use Canva, CapCut, or similar to make images and cut short-form video so that routine content ships without waiting on a design queue. You'll partner with Design on higher-craft, campaign-level work and on reusable templates for recurring post types.
* Build repeatable content series and consistent visual formats rather than one-off posts.
* Publish across LinkedIn, X, Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube, adapting format and framing to each platform rather than cross-posting. You will have a point of view on what content should go on each channel.
* Monitor and evaluate additional or emerging channels and make recommendations about where we should activate.

**Speed On Moments that Matter**

* For events, launches, and known milestones, have content and creative prepared in advance so posts can happen in the moment.
* Cover live moments such as keynotes, events, internal all-hands, offsites, etc. yourself and capture raw video and photos to capitalize on those moments and momentum quickly.
* Monitor news, industry reports, and cultural moments for places our brands and executives can credibly add something.

**Executive And Employee Social**

* Draft, schedule, and manage social content for select senior leaders.
* Identify commentary opportunities where an executive perspective lands better than a brand post.
* Run the employee advocacy program end to end: recruit participants, supply content people actually want to share, and grow participation.

**Measurement**

* Own the numbers. Define the KPIs that matter per channel and per brand, and report monthly on what performed, what didn't, and what you're changing as a result.
* Identify top-performing posts each month and use format testing to make deliberate decisions rather than posting on habit. More volume is not the goal; engagement and impact are.
* Use Sprout Social, Google Analytics, and potentially additional tools to inform reporting.

**Brand Safety And Standards**

* Every post gets a human read for accuracy, relevance, messaging alignment, and voice before it goes out. Attention detail is a must.
Uphold brand standards across all social touchpoints, monitor for social media policy issues, and partner with PR and Community on crisis response.  

  

**Who You Are**

* 5+ years in social media strategy and content creation, in-house or agency, with B2B tech experience preferred.
* You've owned a program, not just a queue. You've set the agenda somewhere rather than executing someone else's calendar.
* You are genuinely online. You understand LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube as distinct cultures, not as distribution endpoints, and you know how audiences get built.
* A strong, versatile writer who can move between brand voice and executive voice without flattening either.
* Hands-on with short-form video and design tooling such as CapCut, Premiere, DaVinci, Canva, or equivalent. You can shoot on a phone and cut something good.
* Comfortable with analytics and honest about them. You can walk into a room, say a campaign underperformed, and explain what you're doing differently.
* Organized under real load. Multiple brands, multiple calendars, competing stakeholders, and you don't lose the thread.
* Proactive by default. You surface the problem and the proposed fix before someone else notice

**About us**Hipster Inc is a Singapore-based technology company with teams in Singapore and India. We build software for enterprise and government clients, from cloud platforms to AI-powered systems.

We also built Voncierge, our own AI and video customer-service platform. Visitors get help through QR codes, web, app or kiosks, answered by an AI avatar or a live agent over video. Voncierge is live at Changi Airport and Jewel Changi, and we’re in conversations with airports across Asia and North America.

**The role**This is our first senior marketing hire. You’ll own marketing across both businesses, with 60:40 split on Voncierge and Hipster. There’s no playbook waiting for you: you’ll set the strategy, decide where the budget goes, and run it. You’ll report to the CEO and lead a small growth team (a growth manager and an intern).

This is a player-coach role. You’ll set the positioning and also write and ship the campaigns yourself.

**What you’ll own**

* Positioning and messaging for both brands, and how they strengthen each other
* Pipeline: qualified meetings for our business development team, against a target you help set
* Account-based campaigns into airports, government agencies and large enterprises
* Case studies, content and thought leadership that build trust in long sales cycles
* Events and trade shows, from pre-event outreach to post-event follow-up
* Marketing support for proposals and tenders, working with our India-based proposals team
* Our marketing tools (LinkedIn, Apollo, website, CRM) and reporting on what’s working
* Budget, agencies and freelancers

**In your first 90 days**

* Write the marketing plan for both brands and agree targets with the CEO
* Launch your first account-based campaign into a priority sector
* Set up monthly reporting on marketing-sourced pipeline

**You’re a fit if you have**

* 5+ years in B2B marketing, including building marketing from scratch at a company under ~100 people
* A track record of owning a pipeline or revenue number, and you can tell us what it was
* Experience with long, complex sales cycles: enterprise, government or tenders
* Strong writing: you can produce a sharp case study or LinkedIn post yourself
* Comfort using AI tools to get more done with a small team
* The discipline to work independently and remotely, with clear written communication

**Nice to have**

* Background in conversational AI, customer-experience tech, SaaS or IT services
* Exposure to airports, travel or facilities management
* Experience marketing across APAC and North America

**This probably isn’t for you if** you’re used to large budgets and big teams, and you prefer directing agencies to doing the work yourself.

**What we offer**

* Real ownership: your plan, your budget, your calls
* A direct line to the CEO and a voice in company strategy
* Remote work within APAC time zones (GMT+5:30 to GMT+8)
* A product already live at one of the world’s leading airports, so you’re marketing something real
* Room to build and lead a bigger team as we grow

jobs.title: Associate Director / Director, Nonclinical Toxicology
jobs.description:
About The Role

We are seeking an experienced Associate Director or Director of Toxicology
to join our nonclinical development team to support discovery and development programs, with a primary focus on nonclinical study oversight and toxicology. The primary focus of this role is to act as a key scientific and operational interface with external contract research organizations (CROs). The individual in this role will assume primary responsibility for the planning, execution, and monitoring of nonclinical studies, ensuring scientific rigor, data quality, and alignment with program timelines and regulatory expectations. This position requires strong scientific judgment, knowledge of regulatory guidance, effective communication, and the ability to independently manage multiple studies in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment. This role will also contribute to the preparation of nonclinical components of regulatory dossiers related documentation.

This individual will also serve as a scientific and strategic partner to cross-functional project teams, driving the design, execution, and interpretation of nonclinical toxicology studies in support of IND-enabling and lifecycle safety assessment programs. The role requires close collaboration with internal stakeholders (project leaders, DMPK, regulatory affairs, clinical development) as well as direct oversight of external Contract Research Organizations (CROs) conducting GLP and non-GLP toxicology studies.

This is a hands-on, operationally-focused role: the ideal candidate pairs strong scientific judgment with the rigor to keep multiple CRO-run studies on schedule, on budget, and audit-ready.

The level of hire (Associate Director vs. Director) will be determined based on the candidate's experience, scope of responsibility, and demonstrated leadership.

Key Responsibilities

Author, review, and finalize toxicology study protocols, amendments, and study reports in collaboration with CRO partners, ensuring scientific rigor and regulatory compliance.
Interface directly with CROs to scope, place, monitor, and troubleshoot in-life toxicology studies (GMP and non-GMP), including dose range-finding, repeat-dose, safety pharmacology, and specialized studies as needed.
Serve as Study Monitor for in-life toxicology studies, including on-site or virtual monitoring visits, real-time issue resolution, and direct follow-up with CRO study directors to keep studies on track.
Own budget tracking and oversight for assigned studies — reviewing CRO quotes and change orders, monitoring spend against forecast, and flagging deviations to project teams and finance.
Review and interpret toxicology data (clinical pathology, histopathology, TK/PK) to assess safety signals and inform risk assessment and dose selection.
Author and contribute toxicology sections for IND (or CTA) submissions, Investigator's Brochures, and briefing documents; support preparation of responses to health authority questions.
Partner with DMPK, pharmacology, CMC, and clinical teams to integrate toxicology findings into overall program risk/benefit assessments.
Track study timelines, budgets, and deliverables across multiple concurrent CRO-run studies; escalate risks and resolve issues proactively.
Stay current with regulatory guidance (FDA, ICH, EMA) and industry best practices in toxicology and nonclinical safety assessment.
Serve as toxicology representative and strategic partner on multidisciplinary project teams, providing scientific input on nonclinical safety strategy from discovery through IND/CTA filing and beyond.

Required Qualifications

S., M.S., Ph.D., DVM, or advanced degree in Toxicology, Pharmacology, Veterinary Medicine, or a related biomedical science (or equivalent experience).
5–10 years of relevant experience in toxicology within pharmaceutical, biotech, or CRO settings.
Demonstrated experience writing and reviewing toxicology study plans/protocols and final study reports.
Direct experience managing or interfacing with CROs conducting in-life toxicology studies.
Experience serving as Study Monitor on GMP toxicology studies, including in-life visits, protocol/report review, and direct communication with CRO study directors.
Working knowledge of study budgets — able to review CRO quotes/change orders, track spend against budget, and flag scope or cost deviations to project teams.
Solid understanding of GMP regulations, ICH guidelines (e.g., M3(R2), S9, S6), and FDA/EMA nonclinical safety expectations.
Demonstrated experience contributing toxicology content to IND submissions (or CTA equivalent), including authoring nonclinical written summaries and supporting health authority interactions.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly convey complex scientific concepts to cross-functional and non-toxicology audiences.
Proven ability to manage multiple projects and timelines in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
DABT (Diplomate, American Board of Toxicology) certification strongly recommended.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience across multiple modalities (small molecule, biologics, ADCs) preferred but not required.
Prior experience in a sponsor-side role managing external vendor relationships.
Experience presenting toxicology data to internal governance committees or health authorities.
Experience with Veeva or other document management systems.

This position is classified as exempt. The anticipated annual base salary range for candidates who will work in San Diego is $207,000 to $243,252. The final base salary offered to the successful candidate will be dependent upon several factors that may include but are not limited to the type and length of experience within the job, and other factors. jobs.title: Water Resources Planner / Scientist
jobs.description:
About Us

We are an award-winning California-based environmental consulting firm with 600+ professionals and more than 30 years of diverse experience serving clients in transportation, energy, water, infrastructure, private development, and government sectors. Our mission is to deliver practical, science-based environmental and planning solutions that support communities, infrastructure, and natural systems. 

As a people-centric organization, we value collaboration, fairness, and transparency, and are committed to fostering a workplace that supports both personal and professional growth while offering robust career opportunities. We are especially proud of our recent Great Place To Work®
certification, which reflects an independent assessment of our culture and our team-member experiences.  

About The Role 

Rincon is seeking a Water Resources Planner/Scientist
with a background in California water supply/reliability, Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA), geology, hydrology, or hydrogeology to support our growing groundwater and water resources practice across California. This role will focus primarily on SGMA planning and implementation, watershed resilience planning, nature-based and groundwater recharge solutions, water resources planning, and grant funding strategies that move water resource solutions from planning toward implementation. Working with Project Managers, Principals-in-Charge, and interdisciplinary technical teams, you will conduct technical research and analysis; analyze groundwater, hydrologic, water quality, and other water resource data; and contribute to technical reports, planning documents, and funding applications. You will also work with public agency clients and interested parties throughout the planning process, helping to gather and evaluate data, support technical analyses, and communicate findings and recommendations. You will have opportunities to build the technical experience needed for greater responsibility and professional growth. 

You will interact with public agency clients, contribute to community outreach and engagement, and help strengthen client relationships through high-quality project delivery. 

We are looking for a motivated, curious, and collaborative professional who is eager to learn and make a tangible impact. This is an opportunity to build technical expertise, work alongside experienced water resources professionals, and help shape the next generation of sustainable and resilient water management across California. 

How We Collaborate 

This role may offer a hybrid work setup, blending time in the office with remote work as business needs evolve. We enjoy coming together in person to collaborate, connect with teammates, and partner with clients, and may prioritize candidates who live within 50 miles of a Rincon office.  
Eligible office locations for this role include Carlsbad, Fresno, Los Angeles, Monterey, Oakland, Palm Springs, Riverside, Sacramento, San Luis Obispo, San Diego, San Jose, Santa Barbara, and Ventura.  

What You’ll Do 

Support SGMA planning and implementation, including Groundwater Sustainability Plans and Alternatives, annual reports, periodic evaluations, plan updates, groundwater monitoring and data analysis, and evaluation of projects and management actions.  
Contribute to watershed resilience and climate adaptation planning by evaluating groundwater and surface water conditions, hydrology, water supply reliability, drought and climate impacts, and opportunities to improve long-term watershed resilience.  
Evaluate nature-based and groundwater sustainability solutions, including managed aquifer recharge, groundwater recharge, habitat and watershed restoration, stormwater capture, and green infrastructure, using geologic, hydrologic, hydrogeologic, and other technical information.  
Support grant applications and funding strategies for groundwater sustainability, recharge, watershed resilience, water supply, recycled water, wastewater, stormwater, and other water resource projects, including evaluating project benefits, readiness, and alignment with funding opportunities.  
Contribute to complex water resources planning documents, including Urban Water Management Plans, Water Shortage Contingency Plans, water supply and recycled water feasibility studies, watershed management plans, technical memoranda, and permitting and funding applications for water/wastewater facilities. 
Conduct technical research, field investigations, and analysis of groundwater, surface water, water supply, water quality, and related geologic and hydrologic conditions to support water resource planning, permitting, and project implementation.  
Prepare materials to support community and governing body engagement related to water resources projects, including drafting e-blasts, social media posts, presentations, resolutions and staff reports, posters, interview/input questions, surveys, and summaries of engagement efforts.   
Analyze and interpret technical data, including groundwater levels, water quality, water use, hydrologic conditions, and other datasets, and translate findings into clear, client-ready technical conclusions and recommendations.  
Prepare technical memoranda, reports, planning documents, presentations, and other materials for public agency clients and interested parties.  
Work collaboratively with hydrogeologists, geologists, engineers, planners, biologists, and other technical specialists and support client and stakeholder meetings, outreach, and project delivery. 

What You’ll Bring 

Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Hydrology, Water Resources, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, or a related technical field.  
Two or more years of relevant professional experience in groundwater, water resources, watershed management, hydrology, environmental planning, or a related field with an emphasis on SGMA and watershed resiliency.  
Foundational understanding of California water resources and interest in groundwater sustainability, water supply/reliability, watershed management, or climate resilience.  
Experience collecting, organizing, analyzing, and interpreting technical or environmental data.  
Strong technical writing and communication skills, with the ability to clearly communicate technical information to a variety of audiences.  
Ability to work collaboratively across technical disciplines, stay organized, and manage multiple assignments and priorities.  
Willingness to learn new technical tools, methods, and regulatory frameworks.  
Intermediate to advanced proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Teams, and other Microsoft products.  
Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record and willingness to conduct fieldwork and travel as project needs require. 

Nice to Have
Masters degree, coursework, or professional experience in geology, hydrogeology, hydrology, groundwater science, or another water-focused technical discipline.  
Experience with or interest in SGMA implementation, including Groundwater Sustainability Plans, annual reports, periodic evaluations, groundwater monitoring, or implementation of groundwater projects and management actions.  
Experience with groundwater or surface water monitoring, inter-connected surface water studies, groundwater dependent ecosystems, hydrologic analysis, water quality, managed aquifer recharge, groundwater-surface water interactions, or watershed assessment.  
Familiarity with California water laws, regulations, and programs, particularly SGMA and water rights.  
Experience with GIS, groundwater or hydrologic datasets, databases, modeling tools, or other technical analytical applications.  
Experience supporting grant applications, funding strategies, or implementation of groundwater, watershed, climate resilience, or water infrastructure projects.  
Professional certification or licensure, such as Professional Geologist (PG) license, Geologist-in-Training (GIT), Professional Engineer (PE), Engineer-in-Training (EIT) certification, or other relevant professional credential, or interest in pursuing professional licensure. 

Investing in You 

The base salary range for this full-time position is $70,000-$95,000
, plus a generous benefits program. Salary ranges are based on the market median of similar jobs, according to third-party salary benchmark surveys. Base pay is determined based on internal equity and a candidate’s job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. 

We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards Package designed to support employee well-being, growth, and financial security. Our benefits are designed to offer flexibility and choice, including health coverage options, employer-sponsored insurance, retirement benefits, generous time off, and programs that support learning, growth, and community engagement. 

Explore more about our culture, benefits, and life at Rincon on our Culture and Benefits page. 

Additional Employment Information 

Individuals offered employment must successfully complete a pre-employment drug screening as a condition of employment. Additionally, those hired who may be assigned to federal projects will be subject to further drug testing, including screening for cannabinoids (THC/marijuana), in compliance with the Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1988 and other applicable federal regulations, which take precedence over California state and local laws.

Eligible office locations for this role include Carlsbad, Fresno, Los Angeles, Monterey, Oakland, Palm Springs, Riverside, Sacramento, San Luis Obispo, San Diego, San Jose, Santa Barbara, and Ventura.  

What You’ll Do 

Lead and manage SGMA planning and implementation, including Groundwater Sustainability Plans (GSPs) and Alternatives, annual reports, periodic evaluations, monitoring programs, evaluation of sustainable management criteria, groundwater projects and management actions, and adaptive management strategies. 
Evaluate complex groundwater and water resource conditions using hydrogeologic, hydrologic, water quality, land use, and climate information, including groundwater levels and storage, water budgets, groundwater-surface water interactions, groundwater dependent ecosystems, and basin sustainability issues. 
Lead or support watershed resilience and climate adaptation efforts, integrating groundwater, surface water, water supply, land use, climate vulnerability, and other technical information to develop practical long-term resilience strategies. 
Evaluate and advance nature-based and groundwater sustainability solutions, including managed aquifer recharge, groundwater recharge, stormwater capture, watershed restoration, green infrastructure, and related water infrastructure, working with multidisciplinary technical teams to assess feasibility, benefits, constraints, and implementation considerations. 
Lead development of grant applications and funding strategies for groundwater sustainability, watershed resilience, recharge, water supply, and other water resource projects, helping clients align technically sound projects with available funding and move priority projects toward implementation. 
Direct and integrate technical work performed by multidisciplinary teams, including groundwater modelers, hydrologists, engineers, geologists, environmental scientists, GIS professionals, and other specialists; review technical analyses and work products for quality, consistency, and defensibility. 
Lead development and QA/QC of complex, multidisciplinary water resources planning documents, including Urban Water Management Plans, Water Shortage Contingency Plans, water supply and recycled water feasibility studies, watershed management plans, technical memoranda, and funding applications. 
Lead development of water supply and demand forecasting models using excel-based decision-support tools, addressing water demand factors, passive and active conservation savings, climate change impacts on water use and supply availability, wastewater and return flow generation, and recycled water/non-potable connections.  
Manage projects and client relationships, including scopes, budgets, schedules, contracts, subcontractors, deliverables, meetings, and multidisciplinary project teams across multiple concurrent assignments. 
Lead planning and facilitation of community and governing body engagement related to water resources projects, including e-blasts, social media posts, presentations, resolutions and staff reports, posters, interview/input sessions, surveys, and summaries of engagement efforts.   
Communicate complex technical information clearly through technical reports and memoranda, presentations, workshops, public meetings, and discussions with Groundwater Sustainability Agencies, water districts, municipalities, state agencies, stakeholders, and other clients. 
Support proposals, client development, and other business development efforts while mentoring and developing early- and mid-career water resources professionals. 

What You’ll Bring 

Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Hydrology, Geological Engineering, Civil or Environmental Engineering, Water Resources, or a closely related technical field. 
Five or more years of relevant professional experience in groundwater, hydrogeology, hydrology, water resources, SGMA planning and implementation, watershed management, or related technical consulting. 
Demonstrated technical understanding of groundwater systems and hydrogeologic principles, with the ability to interpret and critically evaluate groundwater, hydrologic, water quality, and other water resource data. 
Experience with SGMA or technically comparable groundwater management work, including GSP implementation, groundwater assessments, monitoring, water budgets, sustainability evaluations, or projects and management actions. 
Experience managing projects, including scopes, schedules, budgets, technical teams, deliverables, and client communications. 
Ability to understand and work effectively with groundwater models, water budgets, and other technical analyses and modeling outputs, even if numerical modeling is not the candidate's primary specialty. 
Strong technical writing, QA/QC, presentation, and communication skills. 
Experience working directly with public agencies, water agencies, or other water resource clients. 
Working knowledge of California groundwater and water resource regulations and programs. 
Ability to manage multiple concurrent projects and work effectively across technical disciplines. 
Valid driver's license with a clean driving record and willingness to travel and participate in field activities as project needs require. 

Nice to Have
Certified Hydrogeologist (CHG) or Certified Engineering Geologist (CEG). 
Master's degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Hydrology, Geological Engineering, Water Resources, or a closely related technical discipline. 
Significant experience implementing SGMA, including GSPs or Alternatives, annual reports, periodic evaluations, sustainable management criteria, water budgets, monitoring networks, or projects and management actions. 
Experience interpreting groundwater model results and working directly with modelers on model development, calibration, scenarios, water budgets, or decision-support analyses. 
Experience evaluating groundwater-surface water interactions, managed aquifer recharge, subsidence, groundwater dependent ecosystems, water quality, or other SGMA sustainability issues. 
Experience developing and implementing monitoring programs, field investigations, or hydrogeologic studies. 
Experience with GIS, groundwater databases, hydrologic or groundwater modeling tools, or other technical analytical platforms. 
Experience developing successful grant applications or funding strategies for groundwater, watershed, climate resilience, or water infrastructure projects. 
Experience developing water supply and demand forecast models to support long-range water resources planning efforts. 
Demonstrated experience leading client meetings, workshops, technical discussions, and public or stakeholder presentations. 
Experience developing scopes and budgets, preparing proposals, supporting business development, and developing long-term client relationships. 
Experience mentoring geologists, hydrologists, scientists, engineers, or other technical professionals. 

Investing in You 

The base salary range for this full-time position is $100,000-$125,000
, plus a generous benefits program. Salary ranges are based on the market median of similar jobs, according to third-party salary benchmark surveys. Base pay is determined based on internal equity and a candidate’s job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. 

We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards Package designed to support employee well-being, growth, and financial security. Our benefits are designed to offer flexibility and choice, including health coverage options, employer-sponsored insurance, retirement benefits, generous time off, and programs that support learning, growth, and community engagement. 

Explore more about our culture, benefits, and life at Rincon on our Culture and Benefits page. 

Additional Employment Information

Additionally, those hired who may be assigned to federal projects will be subject to further drug testing, including screening for cannabinoids (THC/marijuana), in compliance with the Drug-Free Workplace Act of 1988 and other applicable federal regulations, which take precedence over California state and local laws.

Description/Job Summary

POSITION DESCRIPTION

HGL is currently seeking an Environmental Scientist II to support environmental restoration projects for federal government clients including USEPA, USACE, USAF, NASA, and various agencies across the United States and territories. Projects commonly involve investigation and remediation of sites with groundwater or soil impacted by emerging contaminants (PFAS), chlorinated solvents, and petroleum compounds as well as abandoned mine lands.

The Environmental Scientist II will work out of our Pleasanton, CA office, unless on field assignments. This role requires travel of up to 50%, primarily within the Western US, but may include occasional travel across the US.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

Ensuring field operations are conducted in a safe manner in accordance with project specific Site Safety and Health Plans / Health and Safety Plans.
Participating in field teams for collection of water, soil, soil vapor, surface water and sediment samples utilizing various sampling techniques.
Performing / conducting field subcontractor oversight inclusive of drilling, monitoring well construction, waste transportation and disposal, and heavy equipment operation.
Contributing to the preparation of work plans and project deliverables (e.g., UFP-QAPPs, RI Reports, SSHP/HASPs, power point presentations, and technical memoranda).

Assisting with proposals, cost estimates, and subcontractor procurement.

2+ years of directly related experience in the environmental industry .

Experience with monitoring well drilling, logging, installation and sampling; developing boring logs and review/interpretation of geological boring logs.

Excellent interpersonal communication skills (both written and oral) including the ability to comfortably engage with varying levels of leadership, subcontractors, internal and external stakeholders.

Master’s degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Environmental Science, Geophysics, Geological/geotechnical Engineering or a related field.
HAZWOPER 40-hour training.
Experience as a Task Manager or Field Team Leader for environmental investigations.
Knowledge and experience of CERCLA, DoD, DOE, EPA, and/or RCRA projects.
PFAS sampling or remediation experience.
Experience using generative AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or similar) to improve technical writing, data analysis, research, visualization, or project delivery efficiency.

Physical & Environmental Requirements

PHYSICAL & COGNITIVE REQUIREMENTS

Ability to lift/move/relocate items up to 50 lbs.
Prolonged sitting up to 70% of the time.
Prolonged standing up to 70% of the time.
Walking over uneven or mountainous terrain.
Viewing computer screen for extended periods.
Ability to interpret and analyze visual data (maps, graphs, warning indicators, etc.).
Driving a company or personal vehicle.
Complex problem solving and decision making.
Reading and interpreting technical documents or regulations.
Communicating effectively with clients, team members, and stakeholders.
Managing competing deadlines and shifting priorities.

Must be able to travel up to 50% of the year.
May work in environments with loud noises, dust, or hazardous materials.
Must wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE).
Office work environment.
Potential for longer days up to 12 hours in duration.

At HGL, we share a drive and vision to restore natural resources and provide ongoing stewardship of our environment to benefit present and future generations. **Job Overview:**

APTIM is seeking a motivated entry-level Environmental Scientist to support our portfolio of federal environmental investigation and remediation projects. Projects commonly involve the investigation and remediation of sites with groundwater or soil impacted by chlorinated solvents, petroleum, radiological contaminants, or emerging compounds. The successful candidate will work under the supervision of project managers and partner with other engineers, scientists, geologists, risk assessors, and health physicists.

**Key Responsibilities/Accountabilities:**

* Assist with the collection, documentation, and organization of field data to support project objectives.
* Contribute to the preparation of project work plans and deliverables.
* Assist with the development of technical scopes of work and cost estimates for proposal efforts.
* Develop and maintain spreadsheets, dashboards, and data-tracking tools.
* Assist in the management, analysis, and interpretation of environmental data using statistical analysis and data visualization tools.
* Identify and evaluate environmental risks and recommend remediation strategies to support compliance with federal, state, and local regulations.
* Adhere to established health and safety policies and procedures and execute work in a safe and conscientious manner.

**Basic Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in environmental science or a related scientific discipline (completed or in progress).
* Relevant internship, research, or academic project experience involving environmental investigation, water or wastewater treatment, sustainability, or ecological conservation (0–2 years).

* Must have strong written and oral communication skills.
* Willingness to learn field sampling methods, equipment operation, and environmental data collection procedures.

* Ability to wear and use required PPE.
* Ability to travel to work sites, including overnight travel.
* Valid driver's license.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

jobs.description:
**Have you always wanted to work in a National Park? Are you a passionate, dedicated educator who is enthusiastic about working with youth? NatureBridge offers full-time educator positions with health benefits, housing, and paid time off. Apply today!**

**About the Position**

NatureBridge provides overnight environmental science education experiences for more than 30,000 students and their teachers every year in the world’s best classrooms: our National Parks. Our mission is to connect young people to the science and wonder of the natural world, igniting self-discovery, and inspiring stewardship of the planet. Through our programs, students explore the outdoors, connect with their peers, discover themselves and develop a lasting relationship with science and the environment around them.

**NatureBridge Educator Schedule -** **Video: What is it like to work at NatureBridge?**

Environmental Science Educator (ESE) schedule varies week-to-week. ESEs can expect to deliver environmental science and team-building programs from 9am - 4pm for 3-5 day programs Monday - Friday, with variability during schools’ arrival and departure days. ESEs also run evening programs 2-3 times a week from 6:30pm - 8:30pm. On a regular program day, the ESE receives up to 30 minutes of paid preparation time. ESEs attend regular meetings with other ESEs, and the education and operations teams to discuss program updates and collaborative feedback to the community workplace. In addition to educational responsibilities, ESEs help in other departments when needed or asked.

**Tasks and functions**

During Program:

* Lead multi-day, student-centered, experiential environmental science programs in outdoor settings.
* Facilitate inclusive, culturally relevant instruction that incorporates multiple perspectives and connects learning to students’ lives and communities.
* Engage students in scientific practices through hands-on investigations, while tailoring programming to meet the specific needs of each school group, align with teacher-defined outcomes, and reflect the NatureBridge Theory of Change.
* Follow NatureBridge risk management policies and procedures, and use sound judgment to make decisions and manage risk while managing students’ physical and emotional well-being when leading groups in outdoor settings. Administer and document first aid as necessary and appropriate, and document as required by NatureBridge.
* Foster a supportive, respectful learning environment and model responsible environmental behavior.
* Design and lead evening programs or assist guest presenters and partners, typically twice weekly following the field day.

Outside of Program:

* Serve as an educator on standby when scheduled.
* Assess and document student learning; contribute to program reflection, evaluation and improvement.
* Participate in staff meetings, training sessions, and program debriefs and complete all required paperwork in a timely fashion.
* Maintain gear and contribute to campus stewardship.
* Contribute to fundraising efforts by sharing stories from the field.
* For staff in NatureBridge Housing: Follow all housing policies and co-created community agreements.
* Build respectful, supportive relationships with staff, volunteers, and participants and provide high-quality customer service.
* Support campus operations and organizational goals through additional duties as assigned, such as event support, special projects, and community stewardship.

**Compensation:**

* $17.14/hour, daily and weekly work hours vary based on programming demand.
* On-site housing may be provided as a benefit of employment.
* Medical, dental and vision insurance
* Option for a 403b retirement plan with employer match after six months
* Paid vacation, training days, and sick leave
* Other benefits include Employee Assistance Plan (EAP), Flexible Spending Account (FSA) and more
* See an example of our Golden Gate housing Here. Housing varies by campus.

**Eligibility Requirements and Qualifications**

We are looking for candidates who have:

* At least 1 year of relevant formal or informal teaching experience
* The social and emotional skills to build rapport and positive relationships with people from all backgrounds, abilities, cultures, orientations, identities and communities.
* A demonstrated commitment to equity and inclusion within your teaching and workplace community. We especially encourage you to apply if you have lived experience as a member of (and/or extensive experience working with people from) any communities that are impacted by the historic and current system of oppression that has limited access to environmental education or the outdoors in general.
* The ability to communicate clearly to different groups, including students, coworkers, supervisors and educational partners.
* A desire to learn and grow, and an openness to feedback and coaching.
* Capacity to pivot quickly and manage logistical changes with composure
* A valid **Wilderness First Responder Certification** or a willingness to attain the certification prior to the start date. Tuition aid is available to hired candidates to offset costs of a re/certification.
* The ability and willingness to perform physically challenging work outdoors and in all weather conditions on uneven terrain; able to hike 5-7 miles in uneven terrain
* Ability to work flexible hours and split shifts, including evenings.

**If you are interested in the role and do not meet every requirement listed, please still apply! We are interested in applicants with unique lived experience and skill sets.**

* Employment eligibility is contingent on successful completion of a background check.

**Why should you join the NatureBridge team?**

* We are a mission-driven organization that values your contributions and supports you in making a positive impact on youth and the environment
* You will get to work in a beautiful natural setting with other dedicated educators who are passionate about the environmen

Under the supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), the Environmental Scientist will conduct environmental health inspections on dairy farms and at milk processing and PRMP plants, gather scientific data, research and investigate food safety hazards, collect samples for regulatory surveillance, test pasteurization equipment for proper operation and food safety controls, and provide analytical expertise and reports on specific food safety parameters on dairy farms, milk processing plants, bulk milk haulers and other dairy food and PRMP facilities, including those associated with possible illegal sales of substandard dairy products to California consumers.

  

As an employee of the California Department of Food & Agriculture (CDFA), you are required to perform the “essential functions” of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation. Most of the workday will be spent traveling in a state vehicle to various locations throughout the region.

  

When working outdoors the incumbent may be exposed to extremes in temperature, fumes and gases. The noise level in equipment rooms may be high. Research Data Analyst 1 (5272C), Environmental Science, Policy, and Management #89414 About Berkeley
  
  
At the University of California, Berkeley , we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.
  
  
At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth . We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.
  
  
We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan , which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.
  
  
Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride .
  
  
Departmental Overview
  
  
The Department of Environmental Science, Policy, and Management is home to multidisciplinary research programs that recognize the urgency of the challenges-and the enormous opportunities-that may lead to transformative change. We have award-winning faculty in climate science, biodiversity, environmental policy, land use, and community outreach who are all driven by a collective interest in our environmental future.
  
  
Position Summary
  
  
The Coastal Climate Resilience Lab (PI Rachel Carlson) seeks a Research Data Analyst 1 in the area of remote sensing and geospatial analysis. This is a part-time position (20 hours per week).
  
  
The Research Data Analyst 1 will conduct data analysis supporting two ongoing research collaborations:
  
  
Remote sensing of freshwater plumes in California (PI Carlson and co-PIs Albert Ruhi and Kelly Hondula)
  
Effects of land use and land cover on nearshore marine environments (PI Carlson).
  
  
This position involves preparing and analyzing ecological datasets using established remote sensing and geospatial methods under the direct supervision of other researchers. The Research Data Analyst 1 will apply data science and quantitative modeling methods to map freshwater flux in the marine environment and evaluate interlocking patterns in human-dominated landscapes and benthic ecosystems. This position works in a team to coordinate data cleaning, quality control, and code documentation, complete computational analysis, and prepare data visualizations displaying analytical results for internal review.
  
  
The Research Data Analyst 1 would be based in the research laboratory of PI Dr. Rachel Carlson on the UC Berkeley campus. They would also be co-mentored by Dr. Albert Ruhi (co-PI, ESPM, Berkeley) and remotely by Dr. Kelly Hondula (Arizona State University). They would receive additional guidance from at least one PhD student. Remote working arrangements are considered.
  
  
The Research Data Analyst 1 would have the opportunity to participate in campus data science, wilderness first aid, and other professional development opportunities. They would have the opportunity to attend one USA-based conference each year. The PI's group provides a supportive work environment that recognizes and supports people of diverse identities and needs and prioritizes inclusive practices and field safety.

The First Review Date for this job is October 26, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.

50%
  
  
Under direct supervision, performs basic statistical and data analysis.
  
Apply existing code to new data found from an online repository to deliver code outputs.
  
Apply an existing code script (existing method) to data on inputs to the California coastline.
  
Create reports and basic visualizations on results.
  
  
15%
  
  
Supports testing of research instruments and data sources.
  
Using standard geospatial software/tools and under direct supervision, create a map of tree species using an established method and protocol.
  
  
10%
  
  
Collects research data and prepares it for analysis.
  
  
10%
  
  
Assists with study design proposals and survey instruments.
  
  
5%
  
  
Assists with report preparation and / or analysis for internal constituents.
  
  
5%
  
  
Develops knowledge in areas of storage, documentation and dissemination of computerized data.
  
  
5%
  
  
Assists with evaluation and research of data reporting products.
  
  
Required Qualifications
  
  
Acquiring knowledge of research function. Acquiring ability to perform research analysis duties.
  
Acquiring statistical analysis, systems programming, and database design skills to perform research analysis duties.
  
Ability to effectively manage time and see assigned parts of projects through to completion on deadline.
  
Basic consultation and communication skills.
  
  
Education / Training
